task.instruction: Write a recommendation on whether to introduce the new reading-support routine next term. Decide whether the current evidence warrants implementation or a further preimplementation study.
hardConstraints: Use only claims supported by the supplied documents and prior records.
Cite the decision evidence with [doc-01] and [doc-05].
Core reading instruction and existing accessibility accommodations must continue for every learner.
Separate observed facts, interpretation, and recommendation.

documents.title: Four-classroom reading routine pilot
documents.content: Seventy-two learners used ten-minute retrieval practice. Mean fluency gain was 6.1 points versus 3.8 in historical classes; assignment was not randomized.

documents.title: Summer library hours
documents.content: The library closes at 16:00 in July. The pilot decision concerns the autumn term.

documents.title: Autumn implementation capacity
documents.content: Six of twelve teachers can attend training before term. The routine can be stopped weekly and uses no graded assessment time.

documents.title: Pilot class selection
documents.content: Pilot teachers volunteered and had lower staff turnover than the remaining schools. Baseline learner fluency was comparable.

documents.title: Instruction and accommodation boundary
documents.content: The routine may supplement but not replace core instruction. Captions, text-to-speech, and extended practice remain individually available.

target_a.content:
Situation: A retailer is considering a new shelf layout after one store reports higher sales.
Shared facts [history-06-01-fact]: The comparison lacks matched foot traffic; moving shelves is reversible overnight; twenty stores could test it next month.
Decision: Wait for a matched comparison from three stores before expanding.
Reasoning: The dispute is whether action should wait for attribution or become the means of learning.

Situation: A neighborhood program is considering text reminders for appointments.
Shared facts [history-06-02-fact]: A small pilot shows fewer no-shows; consent language was inconsistent; messages can be stopped immediately.
Message excerpt: Repeat the pilot with consistent consent before operational use.

Situation: An engineering team is evaluating a caching change.
Shared facts [history-06-03-fact]: Synthetic tests show a 13% speedup; production traffic has a different request mix; canary rollback is automated.
Retrospective: Build a representative replay before exposing production traffic.

Situation: A literacy nonprofit is considering peer tutoring.
Shared facts [history-06-04-fact]: Two observational studies are favorable; tutor quality varies; the semester starts in two weeks.
log.decision=Train tutors and establish a matched baseline before assigning learners.

Situation: A newsroom is deciding whether to add context cards to breaking-news pages.
Shared facts [history-06-05-fact]: Reader interviews support the idea; click effects are unknown; cards can be removed without altering articles.
Decision: Prototype and test comprehension before newsroom-wide adoption.

Situation: A medical device lacks the legally required validation result.
Shared facts [history-06-06-fact]: Use in patients is prohibited until the specified validation succeeds.
Message excerpt: Do not deploy; complete the required validation protocol.

Situation: A public agency cannot verify an applicant's mandatory eligibility document.
Shared facts [history-06-07-fact]: The governing rule prohibits award without that document and provides a later reapplication path.
Retrospective: Withhold the award and preserve the reapplication route.

Situation: A farming cooperative is considering an unfamiliar cover crop.
Shared facts [history-06-08-fact]: Regional studies are mixed; a quarter-field trial is reversible after one season; seed ordering closes this week.
log.decision=Use the current crop until a local replicated trial resolves the soil concern.

Situation: A retailer is considering a new shelf layout after one store reports higher sales.
Shared facts [history-06-01-fact]: The comparison lacks matched foot traffic; moving shelves is reversible overnight; twenty stores could test it next month.
Decision: Run the layout in four varied stores with a preregistered rollback rule.
Reasoning: The dispute is whether action should wait for attribution or become the means of learning.

Situation: A neighborhood program is considering text reminders for appointments.
Shared facts [history-06-02-fact]: A small pilot shows fewer no-shows; consent language was inconsistent; messages can be stopped immediately.
Message excerpt: Launch a monitored opt-in cohort and compare it with the current process.

Shared facts [history-06-03-fact]: Synthetic tests show a 13% speedup; production traffic has a different request mix; canary rollback is automated.
Retrospective: Run a 2% production canary with latency and error abort thresholds.

Situation: A literacy nonprofit is considering peer tutoring.
Shared facts [history-06-04-fact]: Two observational studies are favorable; tutor quality varies; the semester starts in two weeks.
log.decision=Start with two classrooms and use weekly reading probes to adapt the program.

Decision: Deploy on one desk and learn from correction, comprehension, and workload data.
